rule: Technical or unfamiliar terms should be understandable where the reader first encounters them and have one canonical glossary entry.

parts.label: Attention
parts.meaning: what attention is directed towards and sustained on

parts.label: Deficit
parts.meaning: part of the historical diagnostic name; it does not mean a person has no attention

parts.label: Hyperactivity
parts.meaning: unusually high activity or restlessness in this context

entries.meaning: ADHD is the abbreviation for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, a neurodevelopmental condition involving patterns of attention, activity and/or impulsivity that can affect everyday life.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: autism
parts.meaning: the current name of a neurodevelopmental condition

entries.meaning: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition associated with differences in social communication, sensory experience, patterns of interest and behaviour, with substantial variation between autistic people.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Alexithymia describes difficulty identifying or describing emotions. It is not the same thing as autism and can occur in autistic and non-autistic people.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Interoception is how the nervous system senses and interprets signals from inside the body, such as hunger, heartbeat, temperature or needing the toilet.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: ism
parts.meaning: a concept, system or theory name

entries.meaning: Monotropism is a theory that describes attention as tending to concentrate deeply on a smaller number of interests or demands at once.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Neurodiversity describes variation in human brains, minds and nervous systems across a population.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: divergence
parts.meaning: difference from a typical or expected pattern

entries.meaning: Neurodivergence is an umbrella term for ways a person's brain or nervous system differs from what is treated as typical. Neurodivergent is the corresponding adjective.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Neurodevelopmental describes conditions or differences involving how the brain and nervous system develop and function.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: typical
parts.meaning: treated as common or expected in a given context

entries.meaning: Neurotype means a pattern of neurological functioning. Neurotypical is commonly used for people whose neurological development is not identified as neurodivergent.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Dyslexia is a learning difference or difficulty mainly affecting accurate and fluent word reading and spelling, with individual profiles varying.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Dyscalculia is a persistent difficulty learning and using number and arithmetic skills; it is not the same as simply being bad at maths.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Dyspraxia is a commonly used name associated with developmental coordination disorder and difficulties with coordination and movement planning.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing. It can affect eating or drinking safety and is different from sensory food preferences or restricted food range.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: Tourette
parts.meaning: an eponym: a name derived from a person's surname

parts.label: syndrome
parts.meaning: a recognised group of features that occur together

entries.meaning: Tourette syndrome is a neurological condition characterised by multiple motor tics and at least one vocal tic over time.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Stimming means repetitive movements, sounds or sensory actions that can serve many functions, including enjoyment, expression or regulation.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Masking is when someone changes, suppresses or hides parts of how they naturally communicate or behave to meet social expectations.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: camouflage
parts.meaning: to make something less visible or easier to blend in

entries.meaning: Camouflaging is a term used for strategies that make autistic or other neurodivergent differences less visible in social situations. It overlaps with, but is not always identical to, masking.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Executive functions are mental processes involved in starting, planning, organising, switching, remembering goals and regulating actions.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: processing
parts.meaning: taking in, organising and responding to information

entries.meaning: Sensory processing describes how the nervous system receives, organises and responds to sensory information.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: overload
parts.meaning: more input than can be comfortably handled

entries.meaning: Sensory overload is when sensory input becomes overwhelming or difficult to manage; what causes it varies by person and context.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: DCD
parts.meaning: the abbreviation for developmental coordination disorder

entries.meaning: Developmental coordination disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition affecting the learning and performance of coordinated motor skills.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: DLD
parts.meaning: the abbreviation for developmental language disorder

entries.meaning: Developmental language disorder is a persistent difficulty with understanding and/or using spoken language that affects everyday life and is not better explained by another biomedical condition.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: disability
parts.meaning: a lasting impairment or barrier affecting everyday life

entries.meaning: In UK usage, learning disability generally means significantly reduced intellectual ability together with difficulties with everyday adaptive functioning, beginning before adulthood.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: burnout
parts.meaning: severe, lasting exhaustion and reduced capacity in this context

entries.meaning: Autistic burnout is a community and research term for severe, long-lasting exhaustion and reduced capacity reported by some autistic people.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Communication differences include variation in speaking, understanding, timing, non-verbal communication and use of AAC.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: task
parts.meaning: something you intend or need to do

entries.meaning: Task initiation is the step between intending to do something and actually starting it; difficulty here can have many causes.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: Communication
parts.meaning: sharing information, needs, thoughts or feelings

entries.meaning: AAC means augmentative and alternative communication: methods that supplement or replace speech, including communication boards, symbols, typing and speech-generating devices.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: Avoidant
parts.meaning: avoiding or staying away from something

entries.meaning: ARFID means avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder, an eating disorder involving restricted food intake for reasons that are not primarily about body weight or shape.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: Special
parts.meaning: requiring provision beyond ordinary arrangements in this context

entries.meaning: SEND means special educational needs and disabilities, a term used in England's education system.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: Pathological / pervasive
parts.meaning: wording used in different versions of the label

parts.label: Demand
parts.meaning: a request, expectation or perceived requirement

entries.meaning: PDA is a contested label for a profile involving marked demand avoidance. Different organisations use different expansions and the term is not a standalone diagnosis in major diagnostic manuals.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: Stress
parts.meaning: the body's and mind's response to threat or strain

entries.meaning: PTSD means post-traumatic stress disorder, a mental-health condition that can develop after traumatic events.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: melatonin
parts.meaning: a hormone involved in signalling biological night and sleep timing

entries.meaning: Melatonin is a hormone produced by the body that helps regulate sleep-wake timing; it is also used as a medicine in some circumstances.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Circadian describes biological rhythms that follow an approximately 24-hour cycle, including the sleep-wake rhythm.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Proprioceptive information tells the brain about body position, movement and force from muscles and joints.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: vestibular
parts.meaning: connected with the inner-ear balance and movement system

entries.meaning: Vestibular information contributes to balance, head movement and the sense of motion and spatial orientation.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Hyperreactivity means responding unusually strongly to sensory input or another stimulus in the context being discussed.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Hyporeactivity means responding less strongly than expected to sensory input or another stimulus in the context being discussed.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Hyperactivity describes unusually high levels of activity or restlessness in the context being discussed; in ADHD it forms part of one symptom domain.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: impulse
parts.meaning: an urge or action that happens quickly

entries.meaning: Impulsivity describes acting or responding quickly without enough time for consideration, in the context being discussed.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Co-occurrence means two or more conditions, traits or experiences are present in the same person or group. It does not by itself say that one causes another.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: heterogeneity
parts.meaning: variation within a group rather than everyone being the same

entries.meaning: Heterogeneity means substantial variation within a group. Heterogeneous is the adjective.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: psychology
parts.meaning: study of mind, behaviour and mental processes

entries.meaning: Neuropsychology examines relationships between brain function, cognition and behaviour. Neuropsychological usually describes assessment or evidence in that field.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Transdiagnostic means an idea, feature or approach that cuts across more than one diagnostic category rather than belonging to only one.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: meta
parts.meaning: combining or examining across studies in this context

entries.meaning: A meta-analysis statistically combines results from multiple studies that address sufficiently similar questions.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: longitudinal
parts.meaning: following the same people, groups or measurements over time

entries.meaning: A longitudinal study observes change over time rather than measuring only a single point.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Psychometric describes the measurement properties of tests or questionnaires, such as how reliably or validly they measure what they claim to measure.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: disciplinary
parts.meaning: connected with professional fields or disciplines

entries.meaning: Multidisciplinary means involving people from more than one professional discipline or area of expertise.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: occupational
parts.meaning: connected with everyday activities and participation, not only paid work

parts.label: therapy
parts.meaning: professional support intended to improve function or participation

entries.meaning: Occupational therapy supports people to take part in everyday activities that matter to them by addressing skills, environments, routines and barriers.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: review
parts.meaning: bringing together and assessing existing evidence

entries.meaning: A systematic review uses predefined methods to find, assess and synthesise relevant research on a specific question.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: morbidity
parts.meaning: illness or health condition in the historical medical wording

entries.meaning: Comorbidity is a medical term for conditions occurring alongside one another. ND Oracle may prefer co-occurrence when no disease framing is needed.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

parts.label: cognitive
parts.meaning: connected with thinking, understanding, attention or memory

parts.label: accessibility
parts.meaning: designing so people can access and use something

entries.meaning: Cognitive accessibility means reducing barriers in information, interfaces or environments for people with different ways of thinking, understanding, remembering or concentrating.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review

entries.meaning: Nonspeaking describes a person who does not use speech, or does not rely on speech, to communicate. It does not mean the person has nothing to communicate.
entries.provenance: ND Oracle governed-corpus terminology accessibility review
